agreement.reference: float32 CPU run, same prompt and seed

boot.recorded_clip: the 30 s clip made by acestep_run.py with --fast all for the same prompt and seed 42 (the clip under evidence in the run log)
boot.fetch: run.sh fetch downloaded the bundle code as real files (21 s)
boot.other_requests: 60 s with a 207-token lyric (seed 7) returned in 1.91 s; 120 s (seed 11) returned in 3.31 s; both passed the 48 kHz sound checks

limits: The planner language model is not loaded, so there is no thinking mode and no audio-code conditioning; the clip follows the caption and lyrics only.

The tokeniser, the sampler update and wavelet correction, the peak normalisation and the WAV write run on the CPU: 0.07 s of a 30 s request and 0.96 s of a 480 s request (the median total minus the two chip stages, which also contains the host-side mask and rotary tables of each clip).

The text encoder, the lyric encoder and the cross-attention projection run on the chip in bfloat16. They are ports in `runtime/acestep_chip.py` that replace methods of the bundle at run time; the bundle's files are not edited. They add a conditioning error of the size of a bfloat16 run (relative L2 about 0.02 for the text encoder). A request with several items or a padded lyric mask uses the CPU path for the lyric encoder.
Text and lyric sequences are padded to a multiple of 128 tokens. A prompt or lyric that needs a new length compiles that shape on first use and takes several seconds longer.
One request runs at a time. The first request at a new duration compiles kernels and takes several seconds longer.
Seeds do not reproduce across backends: a chip clip and a CPU clip of the same seed are different music of the same kind.
The longest clip measured is 480 s.
not_tested: Whether the music is good, or whether sung words are intelligible. The checks measure length and level only.

Languages other than English and styles other than the prompts listed in the evidence. A lyric of 207 tokens was timed and its lyric-encoder output was compared with the CPU's (relative L2 0.0125), but there is no per-step check with a lyric longer than two lines.
Any machine other than one Blackhole p300c board, and more than one chip.
The XL transformer and the 1.7B planner.
changelog: The text encoder, the lyric encoder and the cross-attention keys and values run on the chip (`runtime/acestep_chip.py`); the timbre encoding of the silence reference, the repeated condition-encoder call and the garbage collector no longer cost time per request (`runtime/acestep_fast.py`). `ACESTEP_FAST=none` runs the bundle path as in 0.1.0.
Numbers re-measured: one warm-up and three timed calls at 30, 60, 120, 240 and 480 s, with the 0.1.0 path measured in the same hour for comparison.
First version (0.1.0): the server, the runtime copied from tt-orchard, the bundle and weight pins, the evidence and the card.
